name: Town of Greenburgh (unincorporated)
gaps: Greenburgh has no separate schedule: bulk rules are written into each district section (§ 285-10 to § 285-24); min frontage is only the general 25 ft street-frontage rule (§ 285-39C(9)), so min_frontage_ft left null
County lists R-10 to R-40 height as 25 ft; current code (amended L.L. 2-2013) says 2 1/2 stories, not to exceed 30 ft
M-10, M-14 and M-22 set coverage and yards by building type (two-story vs three-story); two-story figures recorded, three-story in notes
PUD has no fixed yards: 25-75 ft perimeter buffer and 50 ft building setback from PUD line; county min lot (108,900 sf) differs from code's 15-acre minimum site
No accessory-apartment (ADU) provision found in Chapter 285
FAR table (§ 285-39D) starts at 5,000 sf lots; smaller lots not covered

wetlands.summary: Ch. 280: wetland/watercourse buffer is 100 ft from the wetland edge or watercourse high-water line (more if DEC or the approval authority designates); buffers are regulated like wetlands and need a wetlands permit.

steep_slopes.summary: Ch. 245: permit to disturb 500+ contiguous sf of slopes 15%+ (steep 15-25%, very steep 25-35%, excessively steep 35%+); Planning Board reviews disturbances of 500 sf or more. § 285-39E also deducts 20/50/75% of steep/very/excessively steep areas and 75% of wetlands from buildable area.

trees.summary: Ch. 260: permit to remove trees > 8 in. DBH, > 4 in. DBH in wetlands/watercourses/buffers, > 6 in. DBH on excessively steep slopes, any tree of significance or designated tree.

stormwater.summary: Ch. 248: SWPPP permit for land disturbance; 'minor' activity is 500 to < 20,000 sf of disturbance on a lot, 'major' is 20,000+ sf.

general.accessory_structures: Detached accessory buildings keep the district's accessory distances from side/rear lot lines (e.g. 12 ft in R-10) and 10 ft from the principal building; max 12 ft high unless specified (§ 285-40B(4)). Decks may project 5 ft into front yards and 4 ft into side yards (min 5 ft from side line) (§ 285-40C).
general.pools: Rear yard only for one-family homes; at least 15 ft from side and rear lot lines, surrounding patio 10 ft from any lot line (§ 285-36G). Tennis courts only on 30,000+ sf lots, 20 ft from side/rear lines (§ 285-36H).
general.notes: Front yard may be reduced to the average of the two nearest buildings within 200 ft on the same side of the street (§ 285-40C(3)). Corner lots: yard opposite the front is the rear yard (§ 285-39C(2)). Flag lots need twice the minimum lot area (§ 285-39C(10)).

R-40.name: R-40 One-Family Residence

max_building_coverage.note: All buildings; principal building max 14%, accessory buildings max 3.5%

max_impervious_coverage.note: Impervious surfaces (gross coverage): buildings, paving, patios, gravel; unenclosed pools and tennis courts excluded

max_floor_area.note: § 285-39D FAR table for one-family dwellings (R-40 to R-5); FAR applied to lot area (table also lists the floor area at each band's minimum). Over 100,000 sf: 11,500 sf unless Planning Board special permit. Gross floor area excludes half-stories, decks, porches and basements whose floor above is < 6 ft above grade; spaces > 16 ft high count twice

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings and off-street parking areas: min distance to side/rear lot lines per district; accessory height 12 ft unless otherwise specified (§ 285-40B(4)); attached accessory buildings follow principal-building rules (§ 285-40C(4)); 10 ft from principal building

R-40.source: § 285-10B Lot and bulk requirements; § 285-39D FAR standards
R-40.notes: One-family dwellings on lots >= 80,000 sf may reach 35 ft (2.5 stories) if yards are at least front 60, one side 36, both sides 80, rear 64 ft

PUD.name: PUD Planned Unit Development
PUD.notes: Min site 15 acres (and enough for 50 units); density = land area / district min lot size less 25%. Perimeter buffer 75 ft (25 ft for single-family, with buildings at least 50 ft from the PUD line); 15 ft between detached houses; 500 sf open space per bedroom
